```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_ggplot2 <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

A study often reports several related comparisons. Whether their p-values are
adjusted, and over which set of hypotheses, is part of the analysis and is
decided in infercalcR. infereportR then shows the stored raw or adjusted
values and keeps the definition of the family attached to every table, text
and plot label. This vignette uses the `PlantGrowth` and `ToothGrowth` data
sets that ship with R.

```{r packages}
library(infercalcR)
library(infereportR)
```

## One result for a family of comparisons

`PlantGrowth` has three groups, which give three pairwise comparisons. Each
one is a Welch two-sample t-test computed by infercalcR. The finished rows are
then combined into a single result with stable row identifiers and explicit
contrast labels, so that the family can be adjusted as a whole.

```{r family}
weight <- PlantGrowth$weight
group <- PlantGrowth$group
spec <- method_spec("t_means_two_independent_welch")

pairs <- data.frame(
  row_id = c("trt1-ctrl", "trt2-ctrl", "trt2-trt1"),
  comparison = c("trt1", "trt2", "trt2"),
  reference = c("ctrl", "ctrl", "trt1")
)

rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs)), function(i) {
  fit <- run_inference(spec,
    x = weight[group == pairs$comparison[i]],
    y = weight[group == pairs$reference[i]])
  result_data(fit)
}))
rows$row_id <- pairs$row_id
rows$variable_id <- "weight"
rows$contrast <- paste(pairs$comparison, "minus", pairs$reference)

unadjusted <- new_inference_result(rows, list(
  method_id = "t_means_two_independent_welch",
  result_id = "plantgrowth-pairwise",
  population = "PlantGrowth: 30 plants, 10 per group"
))
```

The Holm adjustment is a calculation, so it also happens in infercalcR. It is
applied once to the complete declared family:

```{r adjust}
family <- adjust_inference(unadjusted, method = "holm", family_id = "all-pairwise")
```

## Choose the stored p-value

The `p` argument selects which stored p-value is displayed. Nothing is
recalculated; the choice only decides which column feeds `p_display`.

```{r p-choice}
cols <- c("row_id", "contrast", "estimate_display", "p.value", "p.adjusted", "p_display")
report_table(family, p = "raw")[, cols]
report_table(family, p = "adjusted")[, cols]
```

Asking for adjusted values that were never computed is an error rather than a
silent fallback to raw p-values:

```{r p-missing}
try(report_table(unadjusted, p = "adjusted"))
```

## Select rows after adjustment

`rows` picks rows for display. Selecting happens after the adjustment, and the
metadata still describes the full family, including its size and members:

```{r rows}
one <- report_table(family, rows = "trt2-trt1", p = "adjusted")
one[, cols]
str(report_metadata(one)$adjustment)
```

Full text names the adjustment method next to the displayed p-value:

```{r text}
cat(report_text(family, p = "adjusted"), sep = "\n")
```

## Stars and unavailable results

The `stars` preset uses the thresholds 0.05, 0.01, 0.001 and 0.0001:

```{r stars}
stars <- report_text(family, p = "adjusted", style = "stars")
data.frame(row_id = names(stars), label = as.character(stars))
```

A result that could not be computed keeps its status. It never receives stars
or `ns`, and full text states the recorded reason:

```{r unavailable}
incomplete <- new_inference_result(
  data.frame(
    row_id = c("a", "b"), estimand = "mean difference",
    estimate = c(0.8, NA), conf.low = c(0.1, NA), conf.high = c(1.5, NA),
    conf.level = 0.95, p.value = c(0.03, NA), status = c("ok", "undefined"),
    reason = c(NA, "fewer than two observations in one group")
  ),
  list(method_id = "example", result_id = "incomplete")
)
cat(report_text(incomplete, style = "stars"), sep = "\n")
cat(report_text(incomplete), sep = "\n")
```

## Brackets on a plot

The remaining sections need the optional ggplot2 package; their chunks run
only when it is installed.

Each bracket is described by one row of a positions data frame. Coordinates are
in data units. `group1` and `group2` name the endpoints, and `groups` gives the
order of the groups on the discrete axis.

```{r brackets, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Box plots of dried plant weight for ctrl, trt1 and trt2 with three brackets, one per pairwise comparison, each labeled with its Holm-adjusted p-value."}
library(ggplot2)

positions <- data.frame(
  row_id = pairs$row_id,
  group1 = pairs$reference,
  group2 = pairs$comparison,
  y_position = c(6.5, 7.3, 6.9)
)

base <- ggplot(PlantGrowth, aes(group, weight)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Dried weight")

base + stat_inference(family, positions, groups = levels(group),
  p = "adjusted", tip_length = 0.1)
```

Changing the order of the axis moves the brackets but never reverses a
contrast. Below, `trt2` is drawn first, and each label still shows the stored
difference with its original sign, for example `trt2` minus `trt1`:

```{r reordered, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "The same box plots with the group order trt2, trt1, ctrl; each bracket shows the stored difference and its interval."}
reordered <- PlantGrowth
reordered$group <- factor(reordered$group, levels = c("trt2", "trt1", "ctrl"))

ggplot(reordered, aes(group, weight)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
  stat_inference(family, positions, groups = levels(reordered$group),
    label = "estimate_ci", tip_length = 0.1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Dried weight")
```

## Text labels for omnibus tests

An omnibus test has no pair of endpoints, so it is annotated with text only. Its
position gives `x` and `y_position` instead of `group1` and `group2`:

```{r omnibus}
omnibus <- run_inference(method_spec("anova_one_way_welch"),
  x = weight, group = group, result_id = "welch-anova")
report_table(omnibus)[, c("component", "estimand", "statistic_display", "p_display")]
```

```{r omnibus-plot, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Box plots with the three pairwise brackets and a text label for the Welch one-way analysis of means above them."}
pairwise_plot <- base + stat_inference(family, positions, groups = levels(group),
  p = "adjusted", tip_length = 0.1)
text_position <- data.frame(row_id = result_data(omnibus)$row_id,
  x = 2, y_position = 7.7)
annotate_inference(pairwise_plot, omnibus, text_position,
  template = "Welch ANOVA: {p}")
```

`annotate_inference()` adds the same layers as `stat_inference()` but first
checks that the existing plot uses Cartesian coordinates or `coord_flip()`.
Polar and other nonlinear coordinates are rejected.

## Flipped coordinates and transformed scales

Positions are always given in the original data units. With
`scale_y_log10()`, a `y_position` of 100 is drawn at 2 on the log scale,
transformed exactly once. For horizontal plots, adjust the text justification
and leave room for the labels:

```{r flipped, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Horizontal box plots of dried plant weight with the three pairwise brackets and their labels to the right of each bracket."}
pairwise_flipped <- base +
  stat_inference(family, positions, groups = levels(group), p = "adjusted",
    tip_length = 0.1, text_hjust = -0.1, text_vjust = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  coord_flip()
pairwise_flipped
```

## Results per facet

Results that belong to subgroups carry their subgroup key as a column, and the
result metadata declares it in `facet_vars`. Here the two supplements in
`ToothGrowth` are compared separately at each dose:

```{r facets-data}
tg <- ToothGrowth
doses <- sort(unique(tg$dose))
by_dose <- do.call(rbind, lapply(doses, function(d) {
  fit <- run_inference(spec,
    x = tg$len[tg$dose == d & tg$supp == "OJ"],
    y = tg$len[tg$dose == d & tg$supp == "VC"])
  out <- result_data(fit)
  out$dose <- d
  out
}))
by_dose$row_id <- paste0("OJ-VC-dose-", doses)
by_dose$contrast <- "OJ minus VC"

dose_results <- new_inference_result(by_dose, list(
  method_id = "t_means_two_independent_welch",
  result_id = "toothgrowth-by-dose",
  population = "ToothGrowth: 10 animals per supplement and dose",
  facet_vars = "dose"
))
report_table(dose_results)[, c("row_id", "dose", "estimate_display", "p_display")]
```

These three p-values are not adjusted. The positions repeat the facet key, and
it must match the stored rows exactly; a missing or conflicting key is an error
instead of a label copied into every panel:

```{r facets-plot, eval = has_ggplot2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, fig.alt = "Box plots of odontoblast length by supplement in three panels, one per dose, each with a bracket between OJ and VC labeled with its p-value."}
facet_positions <- data.frame(
  row_id = by_dose$row_id, dose = doses,
  group1 = "OJ", group2 = "VC",
  y_position = c(24, 30, 36)
)

ggplot(tg, aes(supp, len)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~dose) +
  stat_inference(dose_results, facet_positions, groups = levels(tg$supp),
    tip_length = 1) +
  labs(x = "Supplement", y = "Odontoblast length")
```

Annotations are placed only where the positions say. Automatic placement,
automatic dodging and free facet scales are not inferred. For dodged groups,
give numeric `xmin` and `xmax` instead of `group1` and `group2`.
